---
title: "SQL reference"
---

Signatures below match `SELECT * FROM duckdb_functions() WHERE function_name LIKE 'duckboost%'` on `build/release/duckdb`, including parameter names. MAP keys come from the parsers in `src/model.cpp` and `src/import.cpp`. Table-macro argument types are NULL in `duckdb_functions()`; the types stated for the table macros are taken from their bodies in `src/duckboost_functions.cpp`.

Every example is a new in-memory database. `LOAD` uses the unsigned extension path relative to the repository root.

## `duckboost_train`

Aggregate. Returns one model JSON `VARCHAR` for the whole input.

```text
duckboost_train(y DOUBLE, features DOUBLE[]) -> VARCHAR
duckboost_train(y DOUBLE, features DOUBLE[], options MAP(VARCHAR, VARCHAR)) -> VARCHAR
duckboost_train(y DOUBLE, features DOUBLE[], weight DOUBLE) -> VARCHAR
duckboost_train(y DOUBLE, features DOUBLE[], weight DOUBLE, options MAP(VARCHAR, VARCHAR)) -> VARCHAR
duckboost_train(y DOUBLE, features DOUBLE[], is_validation BOOLEAN) -> VARCHAR
duckboost_train(y DOUBLE, features DOUBLE[], is_validation BOOLEAN, options MAP(VARCHAR, VARCHAR)) -> VARCHAR
duckboost_train(y DOUBLE, features DOUBLE[], weight DOUBLE, is_validation BOOLEAN) -> VARCHAR
duckboost_train(y DOUBLE, features DOUBLE[], weight DOUBLE, is_validation BOOLEAN, options MAP(VARCHAR, VARCHAR)) -> VARCHAR
```

| Option | Aliases | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `backend` | | `reference` | Preferred public name: `native` (built-in histogram GBDT). Stable aliases: `reference`, `duckboost`, `gbdt`. Vendor: `xgboost` / `xgb`, `lightgbm` / `lgbm` / `lgb`, `catboost` / `cb`. Model JSON still serializes the native backend as `"reference"`. |
| `task` | | `regression` | `regression` (`regressor`, `mse`), `binary` (`classification`, `logistic`, `binomial`), `multiclass` (`multi_class`, `multi-class`, `softmax`) |
| `objective` | `loss` | `squared_error` | Regression loss: `squared_error` (`l2`, `mse`, `reg:squarederror`), `absolute_error` (`mae`, `l1`, `regression_l1`, `reg:absoluteerror`), `quantile` (`pinball`, `reg:quantileerror`), or `expectile`. Legacy task names such as `binary` remain accepted. Non-squared objectives require the native backend and `task=regression`. |
| `quantile_alpha` | `expectile_alpha`, `tau` | `0.5` | Quantile or expectile level in `(0, 1)`. Only valid with those objectives. `alpha` remains an alias for `reg_alpha`. |
| `n_estimators` | `num_boost_round`, `iterations` | `10` | Number of boosting rounds. Must be > 0. |
| `growth_policy` | `grow_policy` | `depthwise` | Tree growth: `depthwise` (`depth_wise`, `levelwise`), loss-guided `lossguide` (`leafwise`, `leaf_wise`, `best_first`), or CatBoost-style `oblivious` (`symmetric`, `depthwise_oblivious`). Oblivious is native-only; lossguide also works with linked LightGBM. |
| `max_leaves` | `num_leaves`, `max_leaf_nodes` | `31` with `lossguide` | Maximum leaves per loss-guided tree. Must be >= 2 and cannot be set with depth-wise or oblivious growth. |
| `max_depth` | `depth` | `3`; unlimited with `lossguide` when omitted | Maximum tree depth. Must be > 0 for depth-wise and oblivious growth. Loss-guided growth accepts `0` for unlimited depth. |
| `learning_rate` | `eta`, `lr` | `0.1` | Must be > 0. |
| `min_samples_leaf` | `min_data_in_leaf` | `1` | Minimum rows in a leaf. |
| `min_child_weight` | | `0` | Minimum sum of hessians in a child (XGBoost-style). |
| `max_bins` | | `256` | Global quantile histogram bins per continuous feature (computed once from training rows). A feature with at most `max_bins + 1` distinct values keeps every midpoint; otherwise thresholds are thinned to `max_bins` quantiles. LightGBM receives it as `max_bin`. |
| `reg_lambda` | `lambda`, `lambda_l2` | `0` | L2 regularization on leaf weights. |
| `reg_alpha` | `alpha`, `lambda_l1` | `0` | L1 regularization on leaf weights. |
| `min_split_gain` | `gamma` | `0` | Minimum loss reduction required to make a split. |
| `subsample` | `bagging_fraction` | `1` | Row subsample ratio per tree in `(0, 1]`. |
| `colsample_bytree` | `colsample`, `feature_fraction` | `1` | Column subsample ratio per tree in `(0, 1]`. |
| `validation_fraction` | `valid_fraction` | `0` | Random hold-out fraction for early stopping. Defaults to `0.2` when `early_stopping_rounds > 0` and this is unset. Cannot be combined with the `is_validation` argument. |
| `early_stopping_rounds` | `early_stopping` | `0` | Stop if the hold-out metric does not improve for this many rounds; keep the best iteration. |
| `seed` | `random_seed` | `0` | RNG seed for subsampling and the random validation hold-out. |
| `class_weight` | `class_weights` | | `balanced` or comma-separated per-class multipliers (binary / multiclass). |
| `n_classes` | `num_class`, `num_classes` | max label + 1 | Multiclass only; ignored for other tasks. Must be >= 2 and greater than every label. Set it when a class is absent from the training rows. |
| `feature_names` | | `f0,f1,...` | Comma-separated names. The count must match the feature width. |
| `categorical_features` | `cat_features`, `categorical_feature` | | Comma-separated feature names or zero-based indices. The native trainer orders categories by local target statistic (`g/h`) and emits `EQUAL` or multi-category `IN` splits. Linked LightGBM maps this to Dataset categoricals; XGBoost / CatBoost train reject it (use import). |

Unknown keys raise `duckboost: unknown train option`. Values are strings inside the MAP.

Optional `is_validation` marks rows for an external validation set (for example `split = 'validation'` from `duckboost_initial_validation_split`). Those rows are held out of fitting and, when `early_stopping_rounds > 0`, drive early stopping. Do not also set `validation_fraction` when any row is true. `NULL` is treated as false; an all-false mask is ignored so `validation_fraction` still works (including via `duckboost_fit` defaults).

Feature `NULL`s become NaN and the native trainer learns a per-split `default_left` missing direction (same idea as XGBoost). Sample `weight` must be non-NULL and `>= 0`.

Regression supports squared-error, absolute-error, quantile, and expectile objectives on the native backend. Absolute-error and quantile trees renew each grown leaf to the weighted median or requested weighted residual quantile. Binary uses logistic loss and requires labels in `{0, 1}`. `duckboost_predict` then returns the class probability, not a 0/1 label.

Multiclass uses softmax cross-entropy and requires integer class indices `0, 1, ..., n_classes - 1` as `y`, so map string classes to integers first (for example with `CASE`). Each boosting round fits one tree per class, so a model has `n_estimators * n_classes` trees. Each class's starting score is the log of its share of the training rows. `duckboost_predict` returns the most likely class index and `duckboost_predict_proba` returns one probability per class. The XGBoost and LightGBM trainers apply the same label rules.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from _helpers.duckrun import show

show("""
LOAD 'build/release/extension/duckboost/duckboost.duckdb_extension';
CREATE TABLE train AS
SELECT i::DOUBLE AS x, (2 * i)::DOUBLE AS y FROM range(12) t(i);
SELECT left(model, 80) AS model_prefix
FROM (
  SELECT duckboost_train(
    y, [x],
    MAP {'task': 'regression', 'n_estimators': '4', 'max_depth': '2', 'feature_names': 'x'}
  ) AS model
  FROM train
);
""")
```

A three-class model: the label is `0`, `1`, or `2`, and the model stores one tree per class per round.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
show("""
LOAD 'build/release/extension/duckboost/duckboost.duckdb_extension';
CREATE TABLE train AS
SELECT (i // 10)::DOUBLE AS y, [i::DOUBLE] AS features FROM range(30) t(i);
CREATE TABLE models AS
SELECT duckboost_train(
  y, features,
  MAP {'task': 'multiclass', 'n_estimators': '5', 'max_depth': '2'}
) AS model
FROM train;
SELECT
  x,
  duckboost_predict(model, [x]) AS class,
  list_transform(duckboost_predict_proba(model, [x]), lambda p: round(p, 3)) AS proba
FROM models, (VALUES (3.0), (14.0), (27.0)) v(x);
""")
```

## `duckboost_predict`

Scalar.

```text
duckboost_predict(model VARCHAR, features DOUBLE[]) -> DOUBLE
```

Regression returns the numeric prediction. Binary returns a probability in `(0, 1)`. Multiclass returns the argmax class index as a double (ties keep the lowest index).

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from _helpers.duckrun import show

show("""
LOAD 'build/release/extension/duckboost/duckboost.duckdb_extension';
CREATE TABLE train AS
SELECT i::DOUBLE AS x, (2 * i)::DOUBLE AS y FROM range(12) t(i);
CREATE TABLE models AS
SELECT duckboost_train(
  y, [x],
  MAP {'n_estimators': '4', 'max_depth': '2', 'feature_names': 'x'}
) AS model
FROM train;
SELECT duckboost_predict(model, [4.0]) AS pred FROM models;
""")
```

## `duckboost_predict_proba`

Scalar.

```text
duckboost_predict_proba(model VARCHAR, features DOUBLE[]) -> DOUBLE[]
```

Regression returns a one-element list holding `duckboost_predict`. Binary returns `[1 - p, p]`. Multiclass returns a softmax over class scores. The multiclass import on [Import model dumps](vignettes/import-dumps.qmd) checks that those values sum to 1.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from _helpers.duckrun import show

show("""
LOAD 'build/release/extension/duckboost/duckboost.duckdb_extension';
CREATE TABLE train AS
SELECT i::DOUBLE AS x, CASE WHEN i > 6 THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END AS y
FROM range(12) t(i);
CREATE TABLE models AS
SELECT duckboost_train(
  y, [x],
  MAP {'task': 'binary', 'n_estimators': '8', 'max_depth': '2', 'feature_names': 'x'}
) AS model
FROM train;
SELECT duckboost_predict_proba(model, [10.0]) AS proba FROM models;
""")
```

## `duckboost_evaluate`

Scalar. One prediction versus one label.

```text
duckboost_evaluate(model VARCHAR, y DOUBLE, features DOUBLE[]) -> DOUBLE
duckboost_evaluate(model VARCHAR, y DOUBLE, features DOUBLE[], options MAP(VARCHAR, VARCHAR)) -> DOUBLE
```

The only option is `metric` (`auto`, `rmse`, `mae`, `pinball` / `quantile`, `expectile`, `accuracy`, `logloss`, `brier_score` / `brier`, `roc_auc_ovr` / `auc_ovr`, `roc_auc_ovo` / `auc_ovo`). Unknown keys raise `duckboost: unknown evaluate option`.

What the scalar function returns for each metric:

| `metric` | Result on that row |
| --- | --- |
| `mae` | Absolute error |
| `pinball`, `quantile` | Pinball loss at the model's objective alpha. |
| `expectile` | Asymmetric squared loss at the model's objective alpha. |
| `accuracy` | `1` if the classification is correct, else `0`. Binary treats probability `>= 0.5` as class 1. Multiclass compares the argmax index. |
| `logloss` | Row log loss. Multiclass uses the probability of the integer label. |
| `brier_score`, `brier` | Row Brier contribution. Binary: `(y - p)²`. Multiclass: `Σ_c (I(y=c) - p_c)²`. |
| `rmse` | Squared-error contribution; take the square root after averaging rows. |
| `roc_auc_ovr`, `auc_ovr`, `roc_auc_ovo`, `auc_ovo` | Not available on the scalar function (dataset-level only). Use `duckboost_evaluate_agg`. |

`auto` selects accuracy for classification and the matching regression loss for regression models.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from _helpers.duckrun import show

show("""
LOAD 'build/release/extension/duckboost/duckboost.duckdb_extension';
CREATE TABLE train AS
SELECT i::DOUBLE AS x, (2 * i)::DOUBLE AS y FROM range(12) t(i);
CREATE TABLE models AS
SELECT duckboost_train(
  y, [x], MAP {'n_estimators': '4', 'max_depth': '2', 'feature_names': 'x'}
) AS model
FROM train;
SELECT
  duckboost_evaluate(model, y, [x]) AS auto_squared_error,
  duckboost_evaluate(model, y, [x], MAP {'metric': 'mae'}) AS abs_error
FROM models, train
WHERE x = 4;
""")
```

## `duckboost_evaluate_agg`

Aggregate. One number for every input row that shares the model.

```text
duckboost_evaluate_agg(model VARCHAR, y DOUBLE, features DOUBLE[]) -> DOUBLE
duckboost_evaluate_agg(model VARCHAR, y DOUBLE, features DOUBLE[], options MAP(VARCHAR, VARCHAR)) -> DOUBLE
```

`metric` defaults to `auto`: the model's training loss for regression, and accuracy for binary and multiclass. `rmse`, `mae`, `pinball` / `quantile`, `expectile`, `logloss`, and `brier_score` are dataset means (RMSE is the square root of the mean squared error). `accuracy` is the fraction of correct rows. Pinball and expectile use the alpha stored in the model.

Classification probability metrics:

| `metric` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `brier_score`, `brier` | Mean Brier score. Binary uses the common `[0, 1]` form `mean((y - p)²)`. Multiclass uses the original sum-over-classes form on `[0, 2]`. |
| `roc_auc_ovr`, `auc_ovr` | Macro-averaged one-vs-rest ROC AUC. Binary is ordinary ROC AUC on the positive-class probability. |
| `roc_auc_ovo`, `auc_ovo` | Macro-averaged one-vs-one ROC AUC (pairwise probabilities `p_a / (p_a + p_b)`). On binary models this matches `roc_auc_ovr`. |

ROC AUC needs both classes present in each binary reduction; otherwise evaluate raises. `model` and `y` cannot be NULL.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from _helpers.duckrun import show

show("""
LOAD 'build/release/extension/duckboost/duckboost.duckdb_extension';
CREATE TABLE train AS
SELECT i::DOUBLE AS x, (2 * i)::DOUBLE AS y FROM range(12) t(i);
CREATE TABLE models AS
SELECT duckboost_train(
  y, [x], MAP {'n_estimators': '4', 'max_depth': '2', 'feature_names': 'x'}
) AS model
FROM train;
SELECT duckboost_evaluate_agg(m.model, t.y, [t.x], MAP {'metric': 'rmse'}) AS rmse
FROM models m, train t;
""")
```

## `duckboost_to_sql`

Scalar. Returns a `SELECT` that scores `table_name`.

```text
duckboost_to_sql(model VARCHAR, table_name VARCHAR, feature_columns VARCHAR[]) -> VARCHAR
duckboost_to_sql(model VARCHAR, table_name VARCHAR, feature_columns VARCHAR[], options MAP(VARCHAR, VARCHAR)) -> VARCHAR
```

| Option | Aliases | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `separate_trees` | | `true` | `true` / `1` / `yes` emits one column per tree and sums them. `false` / `0` / `no` inlines a single expression. |
| `prediction_alias` | `alias` | `prediction` | Output column name. |

`table_name` must be non-empty. `feature_columns` must name at least as many raw features as the model has. Binary predictions are wrapped in a sigmoid. Multiclass export is an argmax over per-class scores. The [train and export](vignettes/train-predict-export.qmd) vignette runs the generated text without calling `duckboost_*`.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from _helpers.duckrun import show

show("""
LOAD 'build/release/extension/duckboost/duckboost.duckdb_extension';
CREATE TABLE train AS
SELECT i::DOUBLE AS x, (2 * i)::DOUBLE AS y FROM range(8) t(i);
CREATE TABLE models AS
SELECT duckboost_train(
  y, [x], MAP {'n_estimators': '2', 'max_depth': '1', 'feature_names': 'x'}
) AS model
FROM train;
SELECT left(duckboost_to_sql(model, 'train', ['x']), 120) AS sql_prefix
FROM models;
""")
```

## `duckboost_import`

Scalar. Returns model JSON.

```text
duckboost_import(backend VARCHAR, dump VARCHAR) -> VARCHAR
duckboost_import(backend VARCHAR, dump VARCHAR, options MAP(VARCHAR, VARCHAR)) -> VARCHAR
```

`backend` uses the same names as `duckboost_train`'s `backend` option. `dump` is XGBoost JSON, LightGBM text, CatBoost JSON, or duckboost's own JSON. See [Import model dumps](vignettes/import-dumps.qmd) for executed fixtures and the option keys (`task`, `base_score`, `learning_rate`, `feature_names`, `n_classes`, plus the aliases parsed in `ImportOptions::FromMap`).

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from _helpers.duckrun import show

show("""
LOAD 'build/release/extension/duckboost/duckboost.duckdb_extension';
SELECT duckboost_predict(model, [1.0]) AS pred
FROM (
  SELECT duckboost_import(
    'xgboost',
    (SELECT content FROM read_text('test/sql/duckboost/data/xgb_stump.json')),
    MAP {'task': 'regression', 'base_score': '0.0'}
  ) AS model
);
""")
```

## `duckboost_importance`

Table function. Returns one row per feature with gain / cover / frequency and a tidy `importance` score (vip-style).

```text
duckboost_importance(model VARCHAR) -> TABLE(...)
duckboost_importance(model VARCHAR, options MAP(VARCHAR, VARCHAR)) -> TABLE(...)
```

| Column | Type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `variable` | `VARCHAR` | Feature name (`feature_names`, else `f0`, `f1`, …) |
| `feature_index` | `BIGINT` | Zero-based feature index |
| `gain` | `DOUBLE` | Sum of split gains (0 for imports without persisted stats) |
| `cover` | `DOUBLE` | Sum of parent hessian mass at splits |
| `frequency` | `BIGINT` | Number of times the feature was used for a split |
| `importance` | `DOUBLE` | Selected metric, normalized to sum to 1 by default |

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `metric` | `gain` | `gain`, `cover`, or `frequency` (aliases `weight` / `count` → frequency). If `metric=gain` but all gains are 0 (typical for imports), frequency is used. |
| `normalize` | `true` | Divide `importance` by the column sum. |
| `include_unused` | `true` | Keep features that never split. |
| `sort` | `importance` | `importance`, `gain`, `cover`, `frequency`, `name`, or `index`. |

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from _helpers.duckrun import show

show("""
LOAD 'build/release/extension/duckboost/duckboost.duckdb_extension';
CREATE TABLE train AS
SELECT i::DOUBLE AS x_signal, ((i * 17) % 11)::DOUBLE AS x_noise, (3.0 * i)::DOUBLE AS y
FROM range(40) t(i);
CREATE TABLE models AS
SELECT duckboost_train(
  y, [x_signal, x_noise],
  MAP {'n_estimators': '20', 'max_depth': '3', 'feature_names': 'x_signal,x_noise', 'seed': '7'}
) AS model
FROM train;
SET VARIABLE trained_model = (SELECT model FROM models);
SELECT variable, round(importance, 3) AS importance, frequency
FROM duckboost_importance(getvariable('trained_model'))
ORDER BY importance DESC;
""")
```

## `duckboost_build_info`

Table function with no arguments. Columns: `name VARCHAR`, `enabled BOOLEAN`, `notes VARCHAR`.

Rows are the compile flags `DUCKBOOST_WITH_XGBOOST`, `DUCKBOOST_WITH_LIGHTGBM`, `DUCKBOOST_WITH_CATBOOST`, and `DUCKBOOST_NATIVE_STUB`, then `native_*_compiled` / `native_*_linked` for each vendor backend. `native_catboost_linked` is always false: CatBoost has no public training C API.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from _helpers.duckrun import show

show("""
LOAD 'build/release/extension/duckboost/duckboost.duckdb_extension';
SELECT name, enabled FROM duckboost_build_info() ORDER BY name;
""")
```

## `duckboost_fit`

Table macro.

```text
duckboost_fit(source, y, features, weight := NULL, is_validation := NULL, options := MAP {})
```

The body is:

```sql
SELECT duckboost_train(y, features, coalesce(weight, 1.0), coalesce(is_validation, false), options) AS model
FROM query_table(source::VARCHAR)
```

Pass the table name as a VARCHAR literal. `y`, `features`, `weight`, and `is_validation` are expressions in that table. Omitting `is_validation` (all false) leaves random `validation_fraction` early stopping available; pass `is_validation := (split = 'validation')` with rows from `duckboost_initial_validation_split` for an external hold-out. The macro's parameter types are NULL in `duckdb_functions()`.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from _helpers.duckrun import show

show("""
LOAD 'build/release/extension/duckboost/duckboost.duckdb_extension';
CREATE TABLE train AS
SELECT i::DOUBLE AS x, (2 * i)::DOUBLE AS y FROM range(12) t(i);
SELECT left(model, 60) AS model_prefix
FROM duckboost_fit(
  'train', y, [x],
  options := MAP {'n_estimators': '4', 'max_depth': '2', 'feature_names': 'x'}
);
""")
```

## `duckboost_score`

Table macro. No default arguments.

```text
duckboost_score(model, source, features)
```

The body is:

```sql
SELECT *, duckboost_predict(model, features) AS prediction
FROM query_table(source::VARCHAR)
```

`model` is a model JSON value (typically a scalar subquery). `source` is a table name. `features` is the feature list expression inside that table.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from _helpers.duckrun import show

show("""
LOAD 'build/release/extension/duckboost/duckboost.duckdb_extension';
CREATE TABLE train AS
SELECT i::DOUBLE AS x, (2 * i)::DOUBLE AS y FROM range(12) t(i);
CREATE TABLE models AS
SELECT duckboost_train(
  y, [x], MAP {'n_estimators': '4', 'max_depth': '2', 'feature_names': 'x'}
) AS model
FROM train;
SELECT * FROM duckboost_score((SELECT model FROM models), 'train', [x])
WHERE x = 4;
""")
```

## `duckboost_initial_split`

Table macro. Adds a `split` column, `'train'` or `'test'`, to every row of `source`. The rsample equivalent is `initial_split()`.

```text
duckboost_initial_split(source, prop := 0.75, strata := NULL, seed := 42)
```

- `source` is a table or view name, as a string.
- `prop` is the training share, strictly between 0 and 1.
- `strata` is a column or expression; each of its values is split in the same proportions, with `round(prop × n)` training rows per value. It must average at least 5 rows per value, so bin numeric columns first, for example `strata := ntile(4) OVER (ORDER BY price)`.
- `seed` picks the split. The same rows and seed give the same split regardless of physical row order.

The assignment is a hash of each row's values, so adding a column or changing a value changes it. Save the result with `CREATE TABLE ... AS`. See [Splitting data and preprocessing](vignettes/split-and-preprocess.qmd).

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from _helpers.duckrun import show

show("""
LOAD 'build/release/extension/duckboost/duckboost.duckdb_extension';
CREATE TABLE t AS SELECT i, i % 2 AS grp FROM range(20) r(i);
SELECT grp, split, count(*) AS n
FROM duckboost_initial_split('t', prop := 0.8, strata := grp)
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY ALL;
""")
```

## `duckboost_initial_validation_split`

Table macro. Adds a `split` column, `'train'`, `'validation'`, or `'test'`. The rsample equivalent is `initial_validation_split()`.

```text
duckboost_initial_validation_split(source, prop := [0.6, 0.2], strata := NULL, seed := 42)
```

`prop` is `[training share, validation share]`. Both must be positive and sum to less than 1; test gets the rest. Per stratum, the first `round(prop[1] × n)` rows are training and the rows up to `round((prop[1] + prop[2]) × n)` are validation. The other arguments behave as in `duckboost_initial_split`.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from _helpers.duckrun import show

show("""
LOAD 'build/release/extension/duckboost/duckboost.duckdb_extension';
CREATE TABLE t AS SELECT i FROM range(20) r(i);
SELECT split, count(*) AS n
FROM duckboost_initial_validation_split('t', prop := [0.5, 0.25])
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY ALL;
""")
```

## `duckboost_vfold`

Table macro. Adds an `INTEGER` `fold` column from 1 to `v`, for v-fold cross-validation. The rsample equivalent is `vfold_cv()`.

```text
duckboost_vfold(source, v := 5, strata := NULL, seed := 42)
```

Rows are dealt to folds in turn, ordered by stratum and then by the seeded hash, so fold sizes differ by at most one row and each stratum is spread evenly. `v` must be between 2 and the number of rows. For fold *k*, fit on `fold <> k` and score `fold = k`. Pass only the training rows, never the test rows.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from _helpers.duckrun import show

show("""
LOAD 'build/release/extension/duckboost/duckboost.duckdb_extension';
CREATE TABLE t AS SELECT i FROM range(11) r(i);
SELECT fold, count(*) AS n
FROM duckboost_vfold('t', v := 3)
GROUP BY fold
ORDER BY fold;
""")
```

## `duckboost_levels`

Scalar macro that wraps an aggregate, so use it like `min` or `avg`.

```text
duckboost_levels(x, min_count := 1)
```

Returns the sorted list of distinct non-`NULL` values of `x` that occur at least `min_count` times. Compute it on the training rows and pass the list to the encoding macros below.

## `duckboost_dummy`

Scalar macro. The recipes equivalent is `step_dummy()`.

```text
duckboost_dummy(x, levels, one_hot := false) -> DOUBLE[]
```

Returns one 0/1 value per level, in the order of `levels`. By default the first level is the reference and gets no entry (*k* − 1 values). `one_hot := true` returns all *k*. Values not in `levels` and `NULL` return all zeros.

## `duckboost_dummy_names`

Scalar macro.

```text
duckboost_dummy_names(prefix, levels, one_hot := false) -> VARCHAR[]
```

The names matching `duckboost_dummy(x, levels, one_hot)`: `prefix || '_' || level`, with characters other than letters, digits, and `_` replaced by `_`. Join them with `array_to_string(..., ',')` for the `feature_names` option.

## `duckboost_integer`

Scalar macro. The recipes equivalent is `step_integer()`.

```text
duckboost_integer(x, levels) -> DOUBLE
```

The 1-based position of `x` in `levels`. `NULL` and values not in `levels` return 0.

## `duckboost_other`

Scalar macro. The recipes equivalent is `step_other()`.

```text
duckboost_other(x, levels, other := 'other')
```

Returns `x` if it is in `levels`, `NULL` if `x` is `NULL`, and `other` otherwise.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from _helpers.duckrun import show

show("""
LOAD 'build/release/extension/duckboost/duckboost.duckdb_extension';
CREATE TABLE t AS FROM (VALUES ('a'), ('a'), ('a'), ('b'), ('b'), ('c'), (NULL)) v(x);
CREATE TABLE prep AS SELECT duckboost_levels(x) AS lv, duckboost_levels(x, min_count := 2) AS common FROM t;
SELECT
  x,
  duckboost_dummy(x, lv) AS dummy,
  duckboost_dummy(x, lv, one_hot := true) AS one_hot,
  duckboost_integer(x, lv) AS integer,
  duckboost_other(x, common) AS pooled
FROM t, prep;
""")
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
from _helpers.duckrun import show

show("""
LOAD 'build/release/extension/duckboost/duckboost.duckdb_extension';
SELECT
  duckboost_dummy_names('island', ['Biscoe', 'Dream', 'Torgersen']) AS dummy_names,
  duckboost_dummy_names('island', ['Biscoe', 'Dream', 'Torgersen'], one_hot := true) AS one_hot_names;
""")
```
